title: List all git subcommands (what git can do)
summary: See the main commands that git offers, such as add, commit and branch, so you can find the right one. This only prints a list and changes nothing.
prerequisites: git must be installed. On macOS, if git is missing, running it opens a pop-up to install the Command Line Tools.

steps.explain: Check that git is installed. A path such as /usr/bin/git means it is installed. Empty output means git is missing.
Print every git subcommand with a one-line description. Commands are grouped; the 'Main Porcelain Commands' group holds the everyday ones such as add, commit, branch and diff.
steps.expect: First line: "See 'git help <command>' to read about a specific subcommand". Then a 'Main Porcelain Commands' heading and one command per line, about 180 lines.

alternatives.explain: Same list, written with the long option form.

steps.explain: Narrow the list to commands that match a word you have in mind. Replace <WORD> with a keyword such as commit, remote or stash.

placeholders.name: WORD
placeholders.description: A keyword to search for in the command names and descriptions.

steps.expect: Only the matching lines, e.g. 'commit   Record changes to the repository' for the word commit.

verify.expect: The first line is "See 'git help <command>' to read about a specific subcommand".

source.title: git manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
